roles.purpose: Own the route-by-route port from `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web` (MVC 5) to `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web.Core` (ASP.NET Core, .NET 10): controllers, Razor views, filters, YARP forwarding and System.Web adapters, plus multi-targeting `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Domain` so both apps share it.
knowledge: `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web/App_Start/RouteConfig.cs` defines the public routes (for example `p/{slug}`); ported routes must keep the same templates.
`src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web/Global.asax.cs` registers filters, routes and bundles; ASP.NET Core replaces them with middleware, endpoint routing and static web assets.
`src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web/App_Start/Startup.Auth.cs` issues the `.Outdoor.Auth` cookie through OWIN; System.Web adapters remote app authentication lets the new host trust it during migration.
Sessions are InProc in `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web/Web.config`; the cart lives there, so the new host reads it through the adapters' remote session.
`src/Contoso.Outdoor.Domain` is .NET Framework only; multi-target it (net48;net10.0) as SDK-style first so both apps share pricing.
checks: `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` pass for the new projects; `tests/Contoso.Outdoor.Tests` still passes in the Windows CI job.
Each ported route returns the same status code, URL, redirects and visible content as the legacy route.
nonNegotiables: Never change a public URL, query string or cookie name.
One legacy controller per task; unported routes stay forwarded by YARP.
roles.modelReason: Porting routes while sharing session and auth with a live legacy app needs reasoning across two frameworks; parity mistakes reach shoppers.

roles.purpose: Own `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Data` (EF6) and its EF Core 10 port in `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Data.Core`: mappings to the existing SQL Server schema, queries and transactions shared by both apps until cutover.
knowledge: `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Data/OutdoorContext.cs` is EF6 code-first; `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Data/Migrations/Configuration.cs` disables automatic migrations, and the database is authoritative.
EF6 conventions differ from EF Core (pluralised table names, cascade deletes, decimal precision); map tables, keys and `HasPrecision(18, 2)` explicitly.
Azure SQL uses `Authentication=Active Directory Default` with the app's managed identity; local development uses the developer's Entra sign-in.
checks: Integration tests run the EF Core context against SQL Server in a container and compare query results with the EF6 context for the same data.
No EF Core or EF6 migration is added before cutover.
nonNegotiables: No schema change the legacy EF6 app cannot read.
No connection string with a password in any committed file.
roles.modelReason: Mapping a known schema is well-specified work; the traps are documented in this role's knowledge.

roles.purpose: Own containerisation and Azure delivery for the new host: `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web.Core/Dockerfile`, Bicep under `infra/`, `azure.yaml`, Container Apps, Azure SQL, Key Vault, managed identity and the GitHub Actions deploy workflow.
knowledge: `.github/workflows/build.yml` builds the legacy solution on windows-latest; the new host gets its own ubuntu job so neither blocks the other.
ASP.NET Core containers listen on 8080 by default since .NET 8; Container Apps ingress targets that port and terminates TLS.
azd reads `azure.yaml`: `azd provision` deploys `infra/main.bicep`, `azd deploy` builds the image, pushes it to Azure Container Registry and updates the container app.
checks: `az bicep build --file infra/main.bicep` succeeds and `azd provision --preview` shows only intended changes.
`docker build` of the new host succeeds and the container answers its health endpoint.
nonNegotiables: No secrets in Bicep parameters, workflows or appsettings.
GitHub Actions authenticate to Azure with OIDC federated credentials, never stored client secrets.
roles.modelReason: Infrastructure as code follows documented patterns; a strong general model with current Azure knowledge is enough, with Microsoft Learn MCP for specifics.

roles.purpose: Review each feature PR for behavior parity with the legacy app, shared-schema safety and Azure security before it merges.
knowledge: The legacy original of every ported controller is in `src/Contoso.Outdoor.Web/Controllers`; compare actions, attributes and views side by side.
checks: Ported actions keep routes, status codes, validation and anti-forgery attributes; the YARP catch-all still forwards every unported route.
The Windows legacy build and the new .NET 10 build both pass.
nonNegotiables: Block a PR that changes a public URL, cookie or the shared schema without a recorded decision in `docs/destination.md`.
roles.modelReason: A different model family from the main implementer gives an independent second opinion at moderate cost.
